---
title: "Classification"
---

Classification estimates the chance that an observation belongs to a category.
Before we fit a classifier, we need a way to connect a probability model to
observed binary outcomes.

## 1. Likelihood and maximum likelihood estimation

**Estimated time:** 20–30 minutes

Use simulated red/blue ticket draws to distinguish probability from
likelihood, compare proposed probabilities, and identify the maximum-
likelihood estimate. This is the same likelihood idea that logistic regression
will use later, without yet fitting a turbine-data model.

[View the notebook](01-likelihood-and-mle.ipynb)

### Interactive playground

**Estimated time:** 10–15 minutes

Generate ticket draws one at a time and watch the likelihood curve accumulate.
Use the maximum of that curve to identify the maximum-likelihood estimate.

[Open the interactive playground](likelihood-playground.qmd)

## 2. Logistic regression and gradient descent

**Estimated time:** 45–60 minutes

Fit a high-CO classification model using turbine inlet temperature (TIT).
Starting from the likelihood idea, build the binary-cross-entropy loss,
calculate its gradient, and use repeated gradient-descent updates to fit the
model.

[View the notebook](02-logistic-regression-gradient-descent.ipynb)

### Interactive explorer

**Estimated time:** 10–15 minutes

Step through the same logistic-regression updates and watch the coefficients
move downhill on the binary-cross-entropy surface.

[Open the interactive explorer](logistic-gradient-descent.qmd)

## 3. Classification metrics, thresholds, and costs

**Estimated time:** 40–50 minutes

Evaluate the high-CO logistic model on held-out turbine observations. Turn
probabilities into alerts, read a confusion matrix, and calculate accuracy,
precision, recall, and F1. Compare alert thresholds and see how operating costs
can change the appropriate decision rule.

[View the notebook](03-classification-metrics.ipynb)

## 4. Ranking, probability quality, and calibration

**Estimated time:** 30–40 minutes

Evaluate the same high-CO probability model without fixing one alert threshold.
Use ROC/AUC to assess ranking, log loss to assess probability quality, and a
reliability diagram to check whether predicted probabilities agree with observed
frequencies.

[View the notebook](04-ranking-and-calibration.ipynb)

### Interactive ROC builder

**Estimated time:** 5–10 minutes

Lower the classification threshold point by point to see how a training-set
ROC curve grows from `(0, 0)` to `(1, 1)`. Inspect the threshold,
false-positive rate, true-positive rate, and the associated counts at any point.

[Open the interactive ROC builder](roc-threshold-builder.qmd)
